name: Piraeus
title: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement Piraeus | Hull Gauging
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Piraeus and Perama for Greek-managed bulk carriers and tankers: renewal survey gauging, CAP and pre-docking UTM.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement and Hull Gauging in Piraeus
intro: Piraeus is where a great deal of the world's dry bulk and tanker tonnage is managed, chartered and repaired, and it is where Greek superintendents most often need gauging at short notice: a bulk carrier heading for its third renewal survey, a tanker preparing for CAP, a second-hand purchase to be checked before the buyer lifts subjects. For UTM in Piraeus we mobilise a team from India to the vessel, whether it lies at the Perama repair quays, in a floating dock or at the outer anchorage.

highlights.h: Fitted to the Greek docking calendar
highlights.p: Technical departments from Akti Miaouli to Glyfada plan dockings months ahead. We fit mobilisation to that calendar, so the team is cleared to travel before the ship reaches Perama or the anchorage, not after.

Ageing Capesize, Panamax and Handysize bulk carriers and crude and product tankers bring the heaviest gauging scopes to Piraeus. We plan readings across holds, ballast tanks and transverse sections to the extent the coming survey sets out.

Many Perama jobs are done afloat at the repair quays, with docking only when the bottom needs attention. We gauge in either setting and flag probable steel renewal early enough for the yard to prepare plate and labour.

port.h: Piraeus: Greek shipowning, ship management and ship repair in one harbour
p: Piraeus is the port of Athens and the commercial heart of Greek shipping. The harbour itself carries three very different trades: ro-pax ferries to the Aegean islands and Crete, which make it one of Europe's busiest passenger ports; cruise ships using it as a home port; and container ships at the piers at Neo Ikonio, a major transhipment hub within the Piraeus Port Authority (PPA) estate. Yet the reason most bulk carriers and tankers appear here has less to do with cargo than with ownership. The superintendents, technical managers and purchasing departments of a large part of the Greek-owned fleet work within a short drive of the port, and they bring ships to where they can attend in person.

Greek owners have long bought second-hand tonnage and traded it hard, so many of the bulk carriers and tankers they control are approaching or past their third renewal survey at about 15 years, and a good number go through a fourth at about 20. Those are the surveys where gauging becomes heavy: on ESP ships the cargo holds, cargo tanks and ballast tanks are measured section by section, and the readings decide how much steel is cropped and renewed. An owner deciding whether a 20-year-old Panamax justifies another five years will usually want a full set of readings before committing to a dock, and Piraeus is where that decision gets made.

Three things keep ships in and around Piraeus long enough to gauge. Afloat repairs at the Perama quays commonly run from days to weeks; floating-dock stays are built around class surveys; and ships waiting for orders, for a sale to close or for a repair slot lie at the anchorages off Piraeus and in the neighbouring Elefsina bay. Inspection demand here is therefore driven less by the cargo a ship carries than by decisions about its future: renew or sell, how much steel, which yard, and whether it will pass the next charterer's vetting.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens around Piraeus and Perama
p: Most hull work, and therefore most thickness gauging in Perama, happens in the ship-repair zone on the western side of the harbour, facing Salamina. The PPA operates floating docks there, and the repair quays are lined with steelwork, piping and machinery contractors. Ships come alongside for afloat repairs, while the docks take vessels needing bottom work, propeller and rudder attention or a docking survey. Because steel renewal at Perama is often fitted around other repair items, gauging done early lets the yard line up plate and welders before the ship is opened up rather than after.

Beyond the repair zone, gauging is done wherever the ship happens to be. Tankers and bulk carriers at the anchorages off Piraeus are reached by launch, and readings can be taken on deck, in empty ballast tanks and in holds that have been cleaned and ventilated. For heavier dockings, managers also look to the two large yards on the Elefsina bay a short distance north-west. Ferries and cruise ships in the main harbour are best gauged during winter lay-up and refit, when tanks, voids and car decks can be opened up.
list: Perama ship repair zone — afloat repairs at the quays, with gauging of decks, hatch coamings, side shell and tanks while other repair work proceeds
PPA floating docks at Perama — docking surveys and bottom work, with bottom shell, bilge and sea chest gauging done while the hull is dry
Piraeus outer anchorage — ships waiting for orders or a repair slot, boarded by launch for pre-docking, pre-purchase or condition gauging
Container piers at Neo Ikonio — ballast tank gauging and scrubber piping checks on container ships during port stays, arranged with the terminal and agent
Passenger and cruise harbour — ro-pax ferries and cruise ships, normally gauged during winter refits when tanks, voids and vehicle decks are accessible
Elefsina bay yards — larger dockings and heavy steel renewal a short drive away, often combined with Piraeus work in one trip

context.h: Regulation, vetting and the Greek management cluster
p: Greece is an EU member state and Piraeus falls under the Paris MoU, with port state control inspections carried out by the Hellenic Coast Guard. Since 1 May 2025 the Mediterranean has been an emission control area for sulphur oxides, so ships here burn 0.10% sulphur fuel or run an exhaust gas cleaning system. Greek owners were among the early adopters of scrubbers on large bulk carriers and tankers, and the wash-water and overboard piping on those installations, now several years in service, corrodes fast wherever linings have broken down. Shipping has also been inside the EU Emissions Trading System since 2024 and FuelEU Maritime since 2025, which occupy commercial departments but do not alter the gauging scope.

The management cluster shapes the work as much as the regulations do. Greek-owned ships fly many flags — Greek, Maltese, Liberian, Marshall Islands and Cypriot among them — and are classed with every major society, so one technical department may handle several class rule sets in the same month. Tankers over about 15 years meet oil-major vetting that frequently asks for a CAP rating, which means gauging in advance of the CAP survey. Superintendents here also want readings they can use commercially: a steel estimate to compare yard offers, or a measured condition picture to support a sale.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Piraeus
jobs.p: Most Piraeus enquiries come from technical managers planning a survey or weighing a commercial decision. The common thread is timing: readings are wanted before the ship is committed to a dock, a charter or a sale, so the scope is agreed early and the team is booked to arrive while the ship is still accessible at the quay, in the dock or at anchor.
list: Pre-docking gauging of a Panamax bulk carrier at the Piraeus anchorage ahead of its third renewal survey, so the owner can estimate steel renewal in holds and topside tanks before choosing a yard.
Fourth renewal survey gauging on a crude tanker in a Perama floating dock, covering transverse sections, deck and bottom plating and the ballast tank structure required for an ESP tanker of that age.
Gauging for CAP on a product tanker past 15 years whose charterer has asked for a rating before extending the time charter.
Pre-purchase condition gauging on a Handysize bulk carrier at anchor, giving the buyer readings on hatch covers, coamings, frames and hold plating before subjects are lifted.
Scrubber wash-water and overboard piping inspection on a Capesize bulk carrier during an afloat repair at the Perama quays.
Winter-refit gauging of a ro-pax ferry's vehicle decks, void spaces and ballast tanks before the summer island season begins.

logistics: The team flies into Athens International Airport Eleftherios Venizelos and continues by road to Perama, the port or the launch landing for the anchorage. Gate passes for the PPA areas and the repair yards, and launch boats for ships at anchor, are arranged through the ship's agent; we send crew lists and technician certificates in advance for ISPS clearance. Greece is in the Schengen area, so each technician needs a Schengen visa issued in India. We plan applications around the docking date and recommend confirming the job as soon as the yard slot is fixed, particularly if the docking may be brought forward.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ship in Perama while it is doing afloat repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Afloat repair at the Perama quays is one of the most common settings for Piraeus work. We coordinate with the yard so that tanks are opened, gas-freed and ventilated in an order that suits both the repair programme and the gauging sequence, and we pass interim readings to the superintendent as each area is finished, so the yard can start preparing renewal steel before the full report is issued.

faqs.q: Our ship will be at the Piraeus anchorage for only a few days. Is that enough for useful gauging?
faqs.a: It depends on the scope and on which spaces can be made safe for entry. A few days at anchor normally covers deck, hatch cover and coaming readings and one or two ballast tanks or holds. For a full renewal-survey scope on an older bulk carrier or tanker, plan the bulk of the gauging in dock or across more than one call, and we will help you split it sensibly.

faqs.q: Do you provide gauging for CAP preparation on Greek-managed tankers?
faqs.a: We provide gauging for CAP work, and Piraeus is where many tanker CAP decisions are taken. The first step is usually a review of the last renewal survey readings and the class records, followed by a targeted plan for the areas most likely to drive the rating: deck plating, bottom structure and the ballast tanks where coatings have broken down.

faqs.q: How far ahead should we book for a Perama docking?
faqs.a: The moment the Perama yard gives you a slot. The team travels from India on Schengen visas, so we need the vessel name, the yard and the expected docking window several weeks ahead to apply. If the slot moves, tell us at once; we can usually re-plan travel without restarting the visa process, provided the new dates fall within the visa's validity.
